translation_notes: prefixes: TOOLKIT_NS->toolkit, OWL->owl, PROV->prov, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, XSD->xsd
g.subjects(RDF.type, RDF.Statement) -> m{ ?stmt rdf:type rdf:Statement }(g), one-step traversal projecting the subject.

the three '(x, p, o) not in g' existence guards -> bool(m{ {x} p {o} }(g)) each, per the trav_existence idiom, kept as three separate islands rather than folded into one multi-pattern m{ } (folding into a join would change which check short-circuits first and would require re-deriving the AND from a single solution set -- not the same program).
g.triples((stmt, PROV.wasDerivedFrom, None)) and g.triples((deriv, TOOLKIT_NS.premise, None)) -> m{ {x} p ?y }(g), the trav_one_step idiom the stratum targets.
every next(g.objects(...), None) -> m{ {x} p ?o }(g).first(): .first() already returns None on an empty solution set, matching next(..., None) exactly.
needed a context shim (helpers.py) for _parse_term, defined a few lines below the extracted region in the source file but not part of it.

fixture.ttl covers two derivations for one reified statement (one premise complete, one missing rdf:object and so excluded), a neighbouring reified statement for a different triple, and a reified statement with no prov:wasDerivedFrom at all (inner zero-solution case); driver.py adds a third call whose (s, p, o) matches no statement at all (outer zero-solution case). explain_triple's first argument is a file path rather than a graph, so the calls are written by hand instead of using the generic fixture= wiring.
